_doc: K22 rules for implementing-terraform-from-spec, read by the plugin's approval gate (core/gate/spec-approval-gate.py), which gates every skill whose directory holds a gate_rules.json. Each setting carries a why; each command rule carries examples that the gate's unit tests check. A rule whose decision is write decides nothing itself: its writes object names what the matched command writes as a side effect (paths relative to the directory it works in, directory_options, file_options, path_options, operands), and the gate judges that like any other write, so it is denied inside the project before approval.
writable_why: Before approval only the plan, its ledger and planning notes may change. .claude/ holds tooling, not product.
approval_why: The skill asks the user to reply 'approve'. Looser words such as 'ok' or 'go' also answer unrelated questions and would unlock edits by accident.

command_rules.why: An apply touches live AWS state and may be hard to reverse; a state edit can orphan real resources. The skill stops at a targeted plan and the operator applies.
command_rules.message: this changes live infrastructure or Terraform state. The skill stops at the targeted plan and the operator applies. Approve only if you want this run now.

command_rules.why: A plan reads live state under whatever AWS profile is active, so the user confirms the account; terraform test runs apply by default and provisions real infrastructure unless its run blocks use command = plan or mock providers.
command_rules.message: this reads live AWS state (plan) or may create real resources (test). Check the AWS profile and account, and that test run blocks use command = plan or mocks, before approving.

command_rules.why: Migrating state moves the source of truth for live resources. -force-copy also enables -migrate-state and answers yes to its prompts (cli/commands/init); Terraform's flags take one or two dashes (Go flag package).
command_rules.message: this migrates Terraform state. Approve only if you intend it.

command_rules.why: init with the backend enabled (the default) initializes the configured backend, so it connects to remote state under whatever AWS profile is active; -backend-config can point it at a production backend. -backend=false (or its alias -cloud=false, any Go boolean false, the last occurrence winning) skips backend initialization (cli/commands/init), and it is how cli/commands/validate prepares a directory for validation.
command_rules.message: this terraform init connects to the configured remote state backend under the active AWS profile. Check the profile, account and backend config before approving; for validation use init -backend=false.

command_rules.why: Planning never touches live AWS state, and the post-apply smoke checks are read-only. A mutating AWS CLI call from the model bypasses Terraform and drifts the state.
command_rules.message: this AWS CLI call can change live resources outside Terraform. Approve only if you intend it.

match: aws iam put-role-policy --role-name r --policy-name p --policy-document file://p.json

command_rules.why: init and get install providers and modules into the working directory's data directory, .terraform/ unless TF_DATA_DIR names another (cli/commands/init; cli/config/environment-variables, TF_DATA_DIR), and workspace new or select records the selection there. -chdir makes Terraform look in the given directory for all files (cli/commands/init). Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in. An eval run (terraform-plan-and-stop) ran init -backend=false in environment/ before approval and left .terraform/ there.
command_rules.message: terraform init, get and workspace new/select write .terraform/ (or $TF_DATA_DIR) in the directory they run in. Before approval read provider schemas from the Registry, or initialise a throwaway root outside the project (copy the root's versions.tf to "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/<slug>-schema", then terraform -chdir="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/<slug>-schema" init -backend=false; write the path with ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}, since an unset $TMPDIR is a target the gate cannot resolve); init in the project waits for the approved plan.

command_rules.why: Terraform "automatically creates or updates the dependency lock file each time you run the terraform init command", and providers lock pre-populates it; the file lives in the root module's directory (language/files/dependency-lock), whatever TF_DATA_DIR says. -lockfile=readonly suppresses the lock file changes (cli/commands/init). Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in.
command_rules.message: this writes .terraform.lock.hcl in the root module directory. Before approval initialise a throwaway root outside the project instead; a provider change is named in the plan and the lock file changes after approval.

command_rules.why: plan -out=FILE saves the plan to FILE, relative to the -chdir directory. Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in. The skill runs its targeted plan after approval.
command_rules.message: this plan writes its -out file in the project. Run the targeted plan after the plan is approved.
